children: , the processor architecture and silicon company, slipped 3.3% to $321.63 at 10.21am ET time on Thursday as investors weighed how much of the AI server boom it can capture. The opportunity is big. The payoff for Arm is still an open question.

AI agents need CPUs to coordinate tasks around the GPUs running models. But the $120 billion server CPU market forecast cited in the coverage comes from AMD, not Arm. Arm has its own route into that market: partner chip designs and its newly launched Arm AGI CPU. More demand for cores could help both businesses, but Arm still has to win deployments and turn them into revenue.

The valuation leaves little room for a slow conversion. At $321.63, the shares stand 65.57% above the GF Value estimate of $194.26. That gap captures the bet investors are making: agentic AI will create enough real chip sales and royalties to justify today's price.

title: Arm Drops 3.3% as More AI Cores Test Royalty Economics
